title: Stalk formula for the derived exchange mate along a closed immersion
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes and $f:X'\to X$ any morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Form the cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_X X'$ with projections $g:Z'\to Z$ and $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the unbounded derived categories of structure-sheaf modules [def-pc-derived-category] and their derived functors [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For $K\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ let $\beta_K:Lf^*Ri_*K\to Ri'_*Lg^*K$ be the mate of $Li'^*Lf^*Ri_*K\cong Lg^*Li^*Ri_*K\to Lg^*K$, using the composition comparisons and the counit [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition, lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general]. Stalks mean ordinary Zariski module stalks applied to complexes [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. For $z'\in Z'$ put $x'=i'(z')$, $z=g(z')$, $x=i(z)=f(x')$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $A=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X',x'}$, and $C=\mathcal O_{Z',z'}$, with all ring maps induced by the square. The canonical map $A\otimes_R B\to C$ is an isomorphism. There are natural isomorphisms in the unbounded derived category $D(B)$ of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$ (Lf^*Ri_*K)_{x'}\cong K_z\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B,\qquad (Ri'_*Lg^*K)_{x'}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{B\to C}(K_z\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C). $$
Under these isomorphisms the morphism $(\beta_K)_{x'}$ is exactly the canonical ring comparison $K_z\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to K_z\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R B)$ of [lem-pc-affine-derived-base-change-comparison-map], with its target restricted to $B$ and then identified using $A\otimes_R B\cong C$. If $x'\notin i'(Z')$, both $(Lf^*Ri_*K)_{x'}$ and $(Ri'_*Lg^*K)_{x'}$ are zero objects. No Tor independence, boundedness or quasi-coherence is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E23, lemma-compare-base-change-closed-immersion, proof: exact closed pushforward and the displayed stalk comparison, before invoking Tor independence. Stalk indices written with x and x prime for ambient points.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ of $x$ and an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ of $x'$ inside $f^{-1}U$. The affine description of a closed immersion gives $i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(R_0/I)$. Apply the closed-ideal base-change diagram with structural morphism $\mathrm{id}_X:X\to X$, closed subscheme $i:Z\to X$, and base change $f:X'\to X$. Its affine clause gives $i'^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}((R_0/I)\otimes_{R_0}B_0)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0/IB_0)$ and $i'$ closed. By the affine stalk localization theorem, writing $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ for $x,x'$, we obtain $R=(R_0)_{\mathfrak p}$, $A=R/IR$, $B=(B_0)_{\mathfrak q}$ and $C=B/IB$, compatibly with the induced maps. Indeed the prime of the quotient is $\mathfrak q/IB_0$, so its local ring is $B/IB$, and the same applies to $A$. The canonical map $A\otimes_R B\to C$ sends $\bar r\otimes b$ to $rb\bmod IB$; its inverse sends $b\bmod IB$ to $1\otimes b$. The tensor balancing relations make both maps well defined and inverse. Thus it is the asserted canonical isomorphism, with no localization factor left over. The same chart shows $i'(Z')=f^{-1}(i(Z))$.

Closed pushforward has stalks $\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}}M_z$ on the image, by the natural germ map of the closed-pushforward-stalk theorem, and zero stalks outside it. Scalar restriction preserves kernels and cokernels: the additive groups and the maps are unchanged. Hence this stalk formula and the stalkwise exactness criterion show that $i_*$ preserves exact sequences of module sheaves. The same argument applies to $i'_*$. Taking kernels and images degreewise shows that both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently, for any representative $P$ of $K$, $Ri_*K$ is represented by $i_*P$: compare $P$ with a K-injective resolution in the definition of derived direct image and apply the exact functor $i_*$. Likewise $Ri'_*$ is termwise $i'_*$. These comparisons are the canonical derived direct-image comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0E23, lemma-compare-base-change-closed-immersion, first three sentences of proof; modules.tex Tag 01AX

proof.text:
Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ representing $K$ on $Z$ and a flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphism $s:E\to i_*P$ on $X$, using the K-flat-resolution theorem twice. By the definition of derived pullback and step 2, $Lf^*Ri_*K$ is represented by $f^*E$, and $Ri'_*Lg^*K$ by $i'_*g^*P$. Pullbacks of these flat-term K-flat complexes are K-flat by the ringed-topos pullback theorem (applied to the small sites of opens). Let $u:i^*E\to P$ be the ordinary adjunct of $s$, and define $v:f^*E\to i'_*g^*P$ to be the ordinary adjunct of
$$i'^*f^*E\ \cong\ g^*i^*E\ \xrightarrow{g^*u}\ g^*P.$$
The comparison in this display is the ordinary pullback composition isomorphism: by the comparison-is-iso theorem the canonical derived composition comparison is the left-derived lift of the composite pullback counits followed by the conjugate of the ordinary composition, so on the K-flat complex $E$ (where those counits are invertible) it is represented by this ordinary isomorphism. The absolute-derived-functor theorem for tensor pullback makes $Li^*$, $Lg^*$, $Li'^*$ total left derived functors of the ordinary pullbacks, with comparison $\epsilon$ invertible on K-flat complexes; so the derived-adjunction counit formula applies, and it shows that $u$, after identifying $E$ with $i_*P$, represents the derived counit $Li^*Ri_*K\to K$. Since $i^*E$ and $P$ are K-flat, $g^*u$ represents its image under $Lg^*$. Apply the same counit formula for $i'$: $v$ therefore represents the derived adjunct of exactly the composite defining $\beta_K$. Thus $Q(v)=\beta_K$ under the two model identifications. This computes the specified mate, rather than merely a morphism with the same endpoints.

Apply the exact stalk functors to these models. Exactness ensures that $s_x:E_x\to(i_*P)_x=P_z$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $R$-complexes. The K-flat stalk criterion makes $E_x$ K-flat over $R$ and $P_z$ K-flat over $A$. The pullback stalk theorem, natural in the module and hence compatible with every differential, gives $(f^*E)_{x'}=E_x\otimes_R B$ and $(g^*P)_{z'}=P_z\otimes_A C$ as complex isomorphisms. The closed-pushforward stalk theorem for $i'$ identifies $(i'_*g^*P)_{x'}$ with the latter complex restricted along $B\to C$. By the K-flat computation of derived tensor these are the two asserted isomorphisms in $D(B)$, valid for the entire complexes, not only their cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 0E23, displayed stalk comparison; cohomology.tex Tag 06YB; sheaves.tex Tags 0098 and 00AE

proof.text:
Compute $v$ in these stalk coordinates. The pullback-unit germ formula sends $e\in E_x$ to $e\otimes1$. Adjunction sends $s$ to $u$, whose stalk map sends $e\otimes a$ to $a\,s_x(e)$. Pulling this map back by $g$ and using the composition comparison sends $(e\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $c\,\bar b\,s_x(e)$, where $\bar b$ is the image of $b$ in $C$. Taking the adjunct back along $i'$ therefore gives
$$v_{x'}:E_x\otimes_R B\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{B\to C}(P_z\otimes_A C),\qquad e\otimes b\longmapsto s_x(e)\otimes\bar b.$$
These formulas commute with the differentials because $s$ is a chain map and all other operations are scalar multiplication; the composition comparison simply reassociates the tensors. With $C=A\otimes_R B$ from step 1, this is precisely $s_x\otimes_R B$ followed by the balanced complex isomorphism $P_z\otimes_R B\cong\operatorname{Res}(P_z\otimes_A(A\otimes_R B))$. The affine-derived-comparison node defines its canonical comparison by this very map for an $A$-K-flat representative $P_z$ and an $R$-K-flat resolution $E_x\to P_z$. Step 3 identifies its localization with $(\beta_K)_{x'}$, proving the asserted equality of derived morphisms. All ordinary stalk maps and units used here are natural. The canonical derived pullback and comparison are independent of the resolutions; hence these identifications and this equality are natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0E23 proof; more-algebra.tex equation-comparison-map preceding Tag 0661; sheaves.tex Tag 0098

proof.text: Finally suppose $x'\notin i'(Z')$. Step 1 gives $f(x')\notin i(Z)$. By closed-pushforward stalks the complex $(i_*P)_{f(x')}$ is zero, so exact stalks make $E_{f(x')}$ acyclic. It is K-flat by the stalk criterion. The pullback stalk formula identifies $(f^*E)_{x'}$ with $E_{f(x')}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,f(x')}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}$, which represents derived tensor of the zero object by step 4's K-flat computation and is therefore zero in the derived category. The target is represented by $i'_*g^*P$, whose stalk is already the zero complex off the closed image. This proves both zero-object assertions. No part of the argument assumed Tor independence, boundedness, or quasi-coherence.
